title: Operating Lanes Playbook for Cycle Capacity and Staff Rotation
creator: Isabel Moreno
description:
Summary:
This ticket codifies an operating-lanes playbook for cycle planning: an explicit policy for how we allocate headcount across core lanes (Committed Work, Critical Bugs/Incidents, Platform / Reliability Investment, and Strategic Bets) and a lightweight staff-rotation pattern to spread knowledge and maintain velocity across teams. The playbook aims to give PMs and ENG leads a repeatable method for sizing cycles, provisioning reserves, and making defensible scope cuts tied to OKRs.

Problem statement:
We regularly over-index on optimistic scope, lack consistent surge rules, and struggle to coordinate cross-functional swaps when emergencies or high-priority renewals surface mid-cycle. This results in unplanned context switching, multi-week delays to key initiatives, and uneven risk exposure across teams.

Proposal (operating lanes):
- Define four lanes with clear budgeted % of team capacity per cycle: Committed (55-65%), Reliability & Ops (10-15%), Strategic Bets (10-20%), Tactical Reserve (10%). Exact percentages vary by team maturity and OKR cadence; provide a baseline and per-team tailoring guide.
- Tactical Reserve is budgeted in engineer-days and fractional FTEs, not tasks; it is held as an explicit capacity hedge that PMs can use for escalations, customer escalations, and late-priority bugs.
- Staff Rotation: create a 2-week rotation window for a 10-20% fraction of engineers to be on an "integration" rotation (knowledge transfer + cross-team pairing) enabling faster context switch and reducing single-threaded risks. Rotation assignments are opt-in and compensated in scope credit for the owning team.

Scope-cut rules (decision matrix):
- If an unplanned high-priority request consumes >50% of Tactical Reserve for two consecutive sprints, trigger an intra-cycle scope review: items in Committed lane will be re-prioritized based on customer impact, revenue risk, and OKR delta; PMs must supply a 30/60/90 impact statement.
- Cut order: (1) Unscheduled stretch items in Committed, (2) Strategic Bets lower than OKR impact threshold, (3) Deferrable reliability improvements with documented mitigation, (4) Non-blocking polish / UX nice-to-have.

Operational playbook artifacts (what this ticket produces):
- A one-page "Operating Lanes" template for cycle planning (Google Doc) and editable spreadsheet that computes capacity buckets per team.
- A rotation roster template and onboarding checklist for rotating engineers.
- An intra-cycle scope review checklist and a simple triage rubric for PM/Eng leads.
- A pre-cycle checklist for staffing commitments and a post-cycle retrospective template focusing on capacity variance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template doc and spreadsheet are published under Confluence and linked in the cycle kickoff playbook.
- At least three pilot teams (infra, console, and embeddings UI) adopt the lanes in Cycle 2025-W12 and provide capacity baselines.
- The rotation roster and checklist are used in pilot teams and a data snapshot (capacity delta, disruptions avoided) is available after run.

Metrics / signals to monitor:
- Planned vs actual capacity by lane (engineering-days) per team.
- Number of intra-cycle scope reviews triggered and time-to-resolution.
- Percentage of incidents that used Tactical Reserve vs required escalation of additional headcount.
- Velocity variance (story points velocity swing) pre/post rotation pilot.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Publish playbook + spreadsheet + sample filled templates; align with ML Platform and Infra leads. (Confluence + Drive links in artifacts below).
- Week 1–2: Pilot with three volunteer teams (Infra, Console, Embeddings UI). Running retrospective at end of week 2.
- Week 3–4: Iterate on templates based on pilot feedback; provide recommended % buckets for small vs. large teams.
- Cycle 2025-W12: Optional org-wide adoption guidance; include in cycle kickoff materials and cadence for monthly check-ins.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams underutilize Tactical Reserve leading to waste. Mitigation: Require PMs to publish a short justification and planned fallback uses before cycle start; track usage and allow reclaim at mid-cycle checkpoint.
- Risk: Rotation decreases short-term throughput. Mitigation: Limit rotation to 10–20% and only for teams with buffer; award scope credit and treat rotation as planned work in committed lane.
- Risk: Overly prescriptive buckets don’t fit specialty teams. Mitigation: Make buckets configurable and include guidance for one-off exceptions with approvals.

Decision log:
- 2025-02-19: Agreed baseline lanes and target % ranges in cross-functional working group (Isabel, Marco, Naomi, Raj).
- 2025-02-25: Platform requested a larger Reliability & Ops floor for infra-heavy teams; accepted 10–15% per-team configurable floor.
- 2025-03-04: Rotation compensation approved: 0.5 sprint worth of scope credit per rotation cycle for owning team.

Next steps / owners:
- Draft templates: Marco Li (owner) — due 2025-03-06 (done).
- Pilot coordination: Naomi Chen (owner) — pilot runs 2025-03-10 -> 2025-03-24.
- Data capture and dashboard: Eng Analytics (ENG-1842) — dashboard to show capacity by lane.

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- We considered a purely point-based reserve (story points) but selected engineer-days to align with capacity billing and to reduce story point inflation games.
- We debated fixed vs. percentage reserve; a percentage baseline plus small absolute floor worked best across team sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Templates published + 3 pilot teams adopt + rotation roster used and data captured.
decision_log: 2025-02-19: lanes baseline agreed; 2025-02-25: reliability floor for infra teams approved; 2025-03-04: rotation compensation approved (0.5 sprint credit).
